milestone: BSC Core v1.5 — Identifiability, Causal Transfer, and Auditable Evidence

claims.statement: AI-assisted research evidence must preserve frozen target identity, separate generation from verification, classify independence, retain material failures, and promote only the claim supported by the applicable evidence lanes.
claims.authority_ceiling: Normative certificate profile only; it does not validate any AI-generated result or establish workflow novelty.

claims.statement: The full eight-field BSC transfer record admits a coherent displayed or double-category construction with proved units, associativity, interchange, and certificate equivalence.
claims.authority_ceiling: Open problem only; no category of full BSC morphisms is asserted.

claims.statement: A BSC causal-transfer certificate should separate observational, interventional, and counterfactual authority and retain claim-local causal assumptions, intervention maps, typed defects, and authority ceilings.
claims.authority_ceiling: Normative causal profile only; no causal model, empirical effect, or counterfactual claim is thereby validated.

claims.statement: For the declared four-state F14 model, the exact minimum intervention cost is 2; both direct and the pair column-plus-row are minimizers, and the tolerant direct report has target oscillation 3/2.
claims.authority_ceiling: Exact finite deterministic fixture only; no external causal or empirical validity is supplied.

claims.statement: For the declared three-node cyclic F15 cap system, synchronous descent preserves verdicts and reaches the retained greatest feasible fixed point; exhaustive cross-checking finds 84 feasible assignments below the initial caps.
claims.authority_ceiling: Exact finite readiness fixture only; shared parsing and model code mean the cross-check is not an independent implementation.

claims.statement: A report identifies a target exactly when equal reports force equal target values, equivalently when the target kernel contains the report kernel and the target factors through the attainable reports.
claims.authority_ceiling: Mathematical theorem under the declared set-theoretic definitions; it does not establish model truth, empirical adequacy, or novelty.

claims.statement: For a finite completion space, an intervention family identifies the target exactly when its distinguished-pair sets cover every target-separated pair.
claims.authority_ceiling: Finite mathematical reduction to target-relative set cover; it does not supply a causal model or a general complexity improvement.

claims.statement: In the declared finite approximate model, adding report constraints or tightening tolerances cannot increase the target oscillation over compatible pairs.
claims.authority_ceiling: Finite monotonicity theorem; real-valued supremum, statistical, and empirical extensions require additional hypotheses.

claims.statement: The joint BSC integration of product readiness, cyclic caps, operational identifiability, causal-transfer discipline, and source-bound certificates is mathematically novel.
claims.authority_ceiling: Recorded primary-source comparison only; universal novelty or priority is not established.

claims.statement: For a fixed active-axis family whose coordinate values are meet-semilattices, readiness inherits coordinatewise meet and greatest-lower-bound laws; with coordinate tops it also inherits top, while mathematical verdict and execution outcome remain separate types.
claims.authority_ceiling: Mathematical theorem for the declared product semantics; no universal readiness vocabulary or scalar ranking is asserted.

claims.statement: A finite monotone cyclic cap system has a greatest feasible fixed point below its initial assignment, and descending synchronous iteration from the initial assignment terminates there.
claims.authority_ceiling: Human-proof-recorded heterogeneous finite cap theorem only; a cyclic fixed point does not ground the truth or independence of circularly dependent evidence.

claims.statement: For a homogeneous cyclic cap system on one complete lattice, the monotone cap step has a greatest feasible fixed point below the initial ceiling; when the vertex set and lattice are finite, descending iteration from top stabilizes at that fixed point.
claims.authority_ceiling: Kernel-checked homogeneous complete-lattice theorem only; it is not the broader heterogeneous theorem and supplies no grounding for circular evidence.
